# sap-AV curated YARA-Forge subset (ROADMAP E2). Read by update.ps1; also read by the unit tests.
#
# One rule per line:   <YARA-Forge rule name>  <category>  <verdict>  [<mitre>]
#   category: infostealer | miner | hacktool | pup
#   verdict:  malicious | suspicious       (infostealer, miner)
#             hacktool                     (hacktool: always PotentiallyUnwanted, never quarantined automatically)
#             pup                          (pup: always PotentiallyUnwanted, never quarantined automatically)
#   mitre:    optional, comma-separated without spaces; default per category (see update.ps1 $CategoryMitre)
#
# Mapping rules (review E1/E3/E4 M2), checked by ThirdPartyRulesTests:
#   - HKTL_ / Hacktool_ / INDICATOR_TOOL_ / Tool_ names are hacktool; PUA_ names are pup.
#   - MAL_ / MALWARE_ / Infostealer_ / Stealer_ / Trojan_ / Crime_ names are never hacktool or pup.
#   - A rule that has a hack-tool name but detects malware (e.g. HKTL_NET_GUID_Njrat) is not vendored at all.
#   - Generic or weak rules (SUSP_, "generic", "unknown") are suspicious, never malicious.
#   - Plain XMRig / Monero-miner software (not a trojanized miner) is pup.

# SIGNATURE_BASE_HKTL_NET_GUID_*              hack-tool names on RATs/miners (Njrat, Asyncrat, Lime_Miner, ...): M2 conflict
